method: The prompt asks for a single JavaScript function in a ```js block. The block is executed in an isolated vm context with a 2 s budget against gold cases (tests/benchmark/lib/coding.js). PASS = all cases; PARTIAL = some; FAIL = none, no code, missing function or runtime error. Requests use depth 'deep' so the bridge's own deep tier (2048 tokens) is measured; the fast tier's 192-token cap cannot hold a function.

items.prompt: Write a JavaScript function nmToKm(nm) that converts nautical miles to kilometres (1 nautical mile = 1.852 km). Return only one ```js code block, no explanation.
Write a JavaScript function kmToNm(km) that converts kilometres to nautical miles (1 nautical mile = 1.852 km). Return only one ```js code block.
Write a JavaScript function passageHours(distanceNm, speedKn) that returns the passage time in hours (distance / speed). If speed is zero or negative return null. Return only one ```js code block.

Write a JavaScript function normalizeHeading(degrees) that returns the heading normalized into the range 0 (inclusive) to 360 (exclusive), handling negative values and values above 360. Return only one ```js code block.
Write a JavaScript function reciprocalBearing(bearing) that returns the reciprocal (opposite) bearing in degrees within 0–359.999. Return only one ```js code block.

Write a JavaScript function fuelRequired(distanceNm, speedKn, consumptionLitresPerHour, marginPercent) that returns the fuel needed in litres: hours = distance/speed, fuel = hours * consumption * (1 + margin/100). Return only one ```js code block.

Write a JavaScript function nmeaChecksum(sentence) that takes an NMEA sentence body without the leading '$' and without the '*' checksum part (for example 'GPGGA,123519,4807.038,N') and returns the two-character uppercase hexadecimal XOR checksum of all characters. Return only one ```js code block.
Write a JavaScript function isValidLatitude(value) that returns true only when value is a finite number between -90 and 90 inclusive. Return only one ```js code block.

Write a JavaScript function hoursToHHMM(hours) that formats a decimal number of hours as 'HH:MM' with zero padding, rounding minutes to the nearest whole minute (for example 12.5 -> '12:30'). Return only one ```js code block.

Write a JavaScript function averageSpeed(legs) where legs is an array of objects {distanceNm, hours}; return total distance divided by total hours, or null when total hours is 0. Return only one ```js code block.
